exact_prompt:
I'm shopping for cottage cheese in the United States.

I eat cottage cheese regularly and want to minimize cost per serving. Which brand should I buy, and why?
reviewed_answer:
My recommendation: Buy Great Value cottage cheese from Walmart, ideally the 48-ounce tub. Among the widely available U.S. options I checked, it offers one of the lowest costs per serving without requiring a warehouse-club membership.

Great Value 4% Small Curd Cottage Cheese, 48 oz

$5.24

About $0.44 per serving

12 servings per tub, ½ cup each; 12 g protein per serving.

View at Walmart

The main reason is simple: larger store-brand tubs cost much less per serving than many national brands. And since you eat cottage cheese regularly, you're more likely to finish a large tub before it spoils.

Why I'd choose Great Value

Low cost: Its 48-ounce tub is the least expensive of the options compared.

Good protein value: It supplies 12 grams of protein per ½-cup serving, about 3.6 cents per gram of protein.

Widely accessible: Walmart has broad national availability, with no paid membership required.

Strong customer reception: The 48-ounce version has an approximately 4.7/5 Walmart rating, although some reviews mention inconsistent texture. 

One caveat: The 48-ounce tub is not necessarily the best value if you waste some. If you cannot reliably finish 12 servings while the cottage cheese remains fresh, buy the 24-ounce Great Value tub instead.

Bottom line: For regular consumption, make Great Value 48 oz at roughly 44–46 cents per serving your price benchmark. Buy another brand when its sale price beats that benchmark, or when you prefer its taste enough to justify the difference.
